title: Mesh Structures Behind Even-Odd Superconvergence
statement: Consider the surface finite-element discretization of the surface Stokes equations on a smooth two-dimensional surface $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^3$, using discrete geometries $\Gamma_h^k=\Phi_h^k(\widehat\Gamma_h)$ obtained from a uniformly refined reference triangulation $\widehat\Gamma_h$ by a piecewise polynomial parametrization $\Phi_h^k$ of degree $k$. Characterize the internal mesh structures that cause the observed superconvergence for even $k$ but not odd $k$. In particular, are mirrored pairs of triangles the essential mechanism, and how can the same parity effect occur when no such pairing is visible?
